subject: general
question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the month of January every year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pongal**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pongal, is also referred to as **Thai Pongal**, is a multi-day **Hindu harvest festival** of South India, particularly in the Tamil community.
 
• It is observed at the start of the month Tai according to the Tamil solar calendar, and this is typically about **January 14.**
 
• Pongal is celebrates the harvest, particularly rice, and marks the beginning of the **sun’s northward journey** (Uttaraayanam).
 
• It includes various **rituals and community activities,** emphasizing gratitude to nature and farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ugadi**

 
 
• Ugadi is celebrated with enthusiasm in **Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana.**
 
• It signifies the beginning of the **New Year according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar.**
 
• The name "Ugadi" is derived from the Sanskrit words "**Yuga" (age) and "Adi" (beginning),** meaning the start of a new age.
 
 
 
• **Gudi Padwa**
 
 
• Gudi Padwa is also known as **Samvatsar Padvo,** celebrated on the first day of the **Chaitra month** in the Hindu calendar.
 
• Marks the **New Year for people in Maharashtra and the Konkan region.**
 
• The name comes from "gudi," meaning flag or emblem of **Lord Brahma, and "padwa,**" meaning the first day of the moon's phase.
 
• According to Hindu mythology,** Lord Brahma created the universe on Gudi Padwa.**
 
 
 
• **Onam**
 
 
• Marks the end of monsoons and welcomes the **harvest season.**
 
• Celebrated for **10 days during the Malayalam month of Chingam.**
 
• The history of the Onam festival dates back to the **Sangam period.**
 
• This festival commemorates the arrival of Asura King Mahabali’s annual visit from Pataal lok.
 
• Various events like **Tripunithura Athachamayam,** **Pookalam- The Floral Decorations & Arrangement.** 
 
• **Pulikali- The Grand Tiger Dance,** and **Vallamkali**-**The Snake Boat Race are done during this festival.**
